issues.issue: Whether $69,880 of 'family support' paid to a former spouse is deductible alimony under Sec. 215
issues.court: Not deductible: payments end 'until both minor children emancipate', a child-related contingency, so Sec. 71(c)(2)(A) treats them as child support; a co-existing remarriage contingency does not help; state-court label and equity irrelevant.
issues.lean: facts.alimonyPaid [{executed 2012-07-25, paid 69,888, childSupport 69,888}] -> alimonyDeduction 0 (expected 0); asFiled adjustments 69,880.
issues.diagnosis: Sec. 71(c)(2)(A) applied: the whole payment ends on the children's emancipation, so all of it is child support (childSupport = paid) and the Sec. 215 deduction is 0. The decisive step (a mixed child/remarriage contingency still triggers (c)(2)(A); state-court label irrelevant) is legal characterisation, encoded as the childSupport fact, not computed. Unexplained: $5,824/month paid vs $4,500 ordered (fn. 2), $69,888 paid vs $69,880 deducted (fn. 3).
issues.snippet: The existence of this child-related contingency triggers the application of section 71(c)(1) and (2)(A) and makes the payments in question nonincludible

notes: Rerun with the alimony fields (402a5fdbb47/f918d6f6fc9): exit 0; alimonyDeduction 0 and accuracyPenalty 0 match. 24,458/69,880 = 0.35000 exactly, but the prior hypothesis that the whole deduction sits in the 2016 MFJ 35% bracket is arithmetically impossible: that bracket is $413,350-$466,950, only $53,600 wide, less than $69,880 (and with the Sec. 68 3% interaction the TI change is still >= $67,784). So the 35% is a blend of rates. SENSITIVITY (scratch only, assumed facts, not findings): MFJ, no dependents, wages W, deficiency = tax with $69,880 adjustment removed. (a) Standard deduction, W 250,000-620,000 step 250 then 368,000-382,000 step 5: deficiency ranges 19,567-27,673; nearest 24,450 (W ~374,000) and 24,503-24,504 (W 381k-404k, exemption phase-out steps); no exact 24,458 found. (b) Itemized $30,000 held fixed (input is post-Sec. 68, held constant as a simplification), W = 500,260-500,270: deficiency exactly 24,458. There AGI 430,380 -> 500,260, TI 400,056 -> 470,260 (Delta 70,204 = 69,880 + 324 exemptions lost to phase-out), crossing 33% (13,294), all of 35% (53,600) and 39.6% (3,310): 4,387.0 + 18,760 + 1,310.8 = 24,457.8 -> 24,458. So the figure is consistent with TI straddling the 35% bracket on both sides with the exemptions phasing out, but the actual income is unknown; this scenario is one of many.
